description: An object that represents an operation in progress and its eventual result or exception, and the default return type of an async method.
Suspends the method until the task completes, returning the thread to the pool meanwhile and resuming the rest of the method as a continuation.
Blocking on an asynchronous operation with `.Result`, `.Wait()` or `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()`, which holds a thread for the whole wait.
The state where every pool thread is busy or blocked, so new work items queue up and latency grows while CPU stays low.
A per-environment scheduler that UI frameworks and classic ASP.NET use to resume continuations on the UI thread or inside a one-thread-at-a-time request context, and that ASP.NET Core does not have.
A struct alternative to `Task<T>` that avoids an allocation when results are often synchronous, to be used only when profiling justifies it and awaited exactly once.
Returns a task that completes when all the given tasks complete, so independent operations run concurrently instead of one after another.
